Chapter 249: 0246 Showgirl and Gaming Big Shot

The audience at this year's ChinaJoy expo was truly in for a feast for the eyes.

Last year, things were still relatively normal. Although beauties were used to attract attention, their attire was "relatively" conservative.

But this year, it was all exposed legs, waists, and arms.

They looked like they wanted to wear bikinis directly on stage!

This trend would only intensify. A few years down the line, some companies would even hold on-site lotteries for lucky audience members to go on stage and touch the showgirls' chests, pushing the boundaries.

"Not bad."

Chen Guiliang looked at his own company's Sanguo Sha booth; the row of beautiful women was indeed a pleasant sight.

They were wearing hot pants and tube tops, with the three large characters "Sanguo Sha" printed on the tops.

Xu Fengyin pouted, feeling extreme contempt for the planner, yet she couldn't stop herself from frequently glancing at the beautiful women. The girl's sexual orientation was a mystery; as long as someone was eye-catching, she liked to look, regardless of whether they were male or female.

She continued to cosplay as Zhen Ji, so she wasn't dressed so revealingly.

Due to her unexpected fame last year, Xu Fengyin now not only served as the company's art director, but she was also a required presence at any major Sanguo Sha event.

As Chen Guiliang looked at the row of beauties, he suddenly spotted a familiar face.

A long-haired girl was standing in front of the Sanguo Sha booth. The other showgirls all wore smiles, but this girl had an expression that screamed "forced to work." She kept a straight face the entire time, didn't smile when handing out flyers, and couldn't even be bothered to say a word. It seemed all she could think about was getting off work early.

Chen Guiliang asked the employee in charge of executing the expo event, "Where did you find these showgirls?"

The employee was a department manager at Youke. "We put an ad on Xiaonei, inviting female students here in Shanghai to sign up. We didn't need to send people over to pick them in advance, we just screened the applicants' photos online, which saved a lot of money. Plus, students are cheaper. We just have to give them a little money and cover a few meals."

"What's the name of that girl who doesn't smile?" Chen Guiliang asked.

The employee said proudly, "President Chen thinks she's pretty too? I personally selected her. I was stunned just by seeing her photos online. Her name is Ding Beili, and she's a student at a vocational high school in Shanghai."

Of course I fucking know her name is Ding Beili!

In another world, she was this year's most popular showgirl. And she blew up beyond the gaming circle; even people who didn't play games knew of her, and her fame even spread from online to traditional newspapers.

However, back then, she was a showgirl hired for Wulin Waizhuan. In order to chase trends and make a quick buck, Perfect World started advertising and hyping the game before it was even finished.

But now, the game adaptation rights for Wulin Waizhuan had been bought by Chen Guiliang, so naturally, Ding Beili hadn't been hired by Perfect World.

Somehow, she had applied through Xiaonei and become a showgirl for Sanguo Sha.

Chen Guiliang instructed, "Sign her to a long-term contract as our showgirl. A five-year contract, billed per appearance. The contract can be at the normal rate, and we can promote her a little. Once she gets famous, proactively give her a raise to make her feel grateful."

"I'll talk to her alone during the meal break," the employee said. "Just an ordinary vocational high school girl, not famous before. It'll definitely be easy to sign her."

Chen Guiliang thought for a moment. This girl would definitely become famous. And just like Xu Fengyin, she would gather a large number of fans in a short time, with ardent followers even creating a personal fan site for her.

Would it be a waste to just sign her as a showgirl?

"Call her over. I want to ask her a few questions alone," Chen Guiliang said.

A thought suddenly popped into the head of the employee in charge of the booth: President Chen has taken a liking to this beauty?

The employee quickly trotted over. "Ding Beili, President Chen wants to see you. Remember to have a good attitude, don't be so cold all the time."

"Oh."

Ding Beili, who had been grudgingly working while waiting for her shift to end, finally showed a hint of excitement on her face.

Of course, she knew who Chen Guiliang was, as she herself was a Xiaonei user.

The other showgirls at the booth cast envious glances her way.

To these female students, Chen Guiliang was undoubtedly a legendary figure. He was exceptionally charismatic—young, rich, and handsome. If they could catch President Chen's eye...

"Hello, President Chen." Ding Beili was a little shy.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Where are you from?"

Ding Beili said, "I'm a Shanghai local."

Chen Guiliang asked again, "What school did you go to? What was your major?"

Ding Beili said, "Shanghai Vocational School of Broadcasting and Television. My major was Film and Television Program Production. I've already graduated, I got my diploma early this month."

She was currently looking for a job and had already posted her resume on recruitment websites.

She wasn't picky about the job description, either, even indicating that she could work as a "receptionist/etiquette hostess."

As a recent vocational high school graduate with no real skills, she would be lucky to find any job at all.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What did you learn in school?"

"Advertisement design and production, radio, film, and television arts." Ding Beili's voice grew smaller and smaller, and she lowered her head guiltily as she spoke.

Because she had only learned the basics of these subjects.

If she were to actually work in her field of study, she could only do odd jobs.

Chen Guiliang said, "How about this. You have a good image and presence. If you're willing to go to Beijing, you can start as a receptionist for Youke Technology. Whenever Youke has an event, you will also have to appear as a showgirl. You'll be paid per appearance for the showgirl work, which won't be part of your receptionist salary."

"I'd have to leave Shanghai?" Ding Beili hesitated.

Chen Guiliang said, "I will help promote you and make you an internet celebrity. But right now, you lack the personal skills, so even if you become famous, it won't last long. I hope that in the future, outside of work, you'll learn hosting skills. As long as you can develop your hosting abilities, you can become Youke's lead host for both internal and external events."

Ding Beili didn't agree immediately, instead saying, "I'll go home and discuss it with my parents."

"Alright," Chen Guiliang nodded.

Ding Beili went back to work.

Xu Fengyin stood in the distance, muttering, "Perv!"

Chen Guiliang called over the employee in charge of PR and laid out a plan to promote Ding Beili.

Why was Ding Beili able to become famous?

Her innocent beauty was one reason, but she needed another hook.

Xu Fengyin's rise to fame last year stemmed from those non-work-related photos taken by passersby—that was the hook. The professional promotion arranged by Chen Guiliang, in contrast, didn't have much of an effect.

The hook for Ding Beili's fame was that she never smiled.

There were hundreds of showgirls at the ChinaJoy expo, and Ding Beili was the only one who didn't smile the entire time.

But she wasn't always stone-faced; sometimes her expression was quite playful.

Like a little sister from next door who had been dragged here to work against her will.

"Hello, President Chen!"

"You are?"

"I'm the founder of Te Rui Games. We've made a game that's now in closed beta. But we're having some trouble with follow-up funding... I know you have a keen eye, President Chen. If you have time, could you come take a look at our booth?"

"Sure."

Chen Guiliang had already met many owners of small companies like this.

His investment in Tao Chenggang's Quanyu Tianxia had now become a celebrated story in the gaming industry.

The small company before him was very shabby. Their rented booth was in an inconspicuous corner. There was only a single pop-up banner for promotion, two or three employees standing guard, and two computers set up for game demos.

"Please take a look, President Chen, this is our game," the founder introduced enthusiastically. "Our company has a total of three partners, all of us are veteran gamers. This is an MMO game, and we originally planned to use a pay-by-the-hour model. But free-to-play games are more suitable for small companies now, so we switched it to a free-to-play online game halfway through..."

One look at the game's interface and Chen Guiliang felt his hopes sink.

How to describe it?

Legend-level graphics.

The graphics were incredibly crude, and the character models also looked like those from Legend.

But as Chen Guiliang played and listened to the introduction, he felt that they had put in a fair amount of effort. At least, they had been serious about designing the game's world-building and quest system.

It was only due to a lack of money that the graphics turned out so poorly.

There were many small companies and games like this one this year, and there would be even more next year!

If Feng Ji hadn't joined Youke Technology, he would have joined a similar small company. He was in charge of planning in-game events and actually managed to turn a shoddy game into a profitable one.

"What do you think, President Chen?" the founder asked with great anticipation.

Chen Guiliang said, "If this game had been launched early last year, then I would have definitely invested. As for now, I'm very sorry..."

It was outdated now.

The man was quite disappointed to hear that, but he still managed to force a smile. "Thank you for coming by in person, President Chen. I hope we'll have a chance to cooperate in the future."

"Your content is very well-thought-out," Chen Guiliang said. "If your next game can innovate in some aspect and offer something refreshingly new, I would be willing to invest then."

"We'll work hard."

"Keep it up."

This was already the 7th game Chen Guiliang had been pulled aside to look at.

Chen Guiliang strolled over to the other booths and soon noticed a large crowd gathered ahead.

Sohu Changyou, Tianlong Babu.

This game was developed very quickly; it entered closed beta after only 8 months of development. Because Charles Zhang kept pushing and pushing!

Last month, Tianlong Babu opened up 1,000 closed beta accounts.

The closed beta revealed a ton of bugs.

Many closed beta players had already quit. Some were still sticking with it and continuously providing feedback to Sohu.

Chen Guiliang saw that Shang Jin was personally promoting Tianlong Babu, so he walked over to greet him. "President Shang, hello!"

"You're the one who can be called President, I'm just a worker." Shang Jin recognized Chen Guiliang at a glance.

The two quickly began to chat, and they spoke directly in their local dialect.

Their hometowns were both "third-front construction" cities from back in the day in Sichuan province.

Shang Jin's father had been a military industrial worker for the third-front construction.

"You've done a great job on this game," Chen Guiliang praised.

Shang Jin sighed, "Ah, don't mention it. The development time was insufficient, we found so many bugs in the closed beta."

It wasn't convenient for him to speak ill of Charles Zhang.

Moreover, compared to Charles Zhang, Shang Jin was more annoyed with the person directly in charge of Sohu Changyou.

Shang Jin was naturally prone to getting caught in internal struggles.

He had previously participated in the development of WPS at Kingsoft, then transferred to develop Fengshen Bang. The two major factions in Kingsoft's gaming division had a terrible relationship, and when Shang Jin couldn't win the fight, he was out.

He joined Sohu last year to make games, and halfway through the development of Tianlong Babu, he ran into internal strife again.

Next year, he would leave Sohu Changyou because of this internal struggle.

In his previous life, Chen Guiliang had worked in the gaming industry; how could he not be familiar with Shang Jin?

After chatting for a few minutes, Chen Guiliang said in a low voice, "Old Shang, if you ever leave Sohu, you can come to my company. If you want to start your own business, I can invest too."

"Are you trying to poach me?" Shang Jin asked with a smile.

Chen Guiliang said, "We're from the same hometown. It's normal for us to work together."

Shang Jin gave a noncommittal response.

Having been burned by internal struggles twice, it was impossible for Shang Jin to join any other company. After leaving Sohu, he would inevitably start his own company and be the boss.

Moreover, with Shang Jin's experience leading the development of Fengshen Bang and Tianlong Babu, he could easily secure tens of millions in investment.

Chen Guiliang's words were just an attempt to get a piece of the action.

The game Shang Jin independently developed, Genghis Khan, brought in 30 million RMB in revenue in its first month!

In the future, many people who didn't play games would often see "Kylin Pictures" at the beginning of movies. That was also something Shang Jin started; his gaming company was called Kylin Games.

Shang Jin was an oddball. At the peak of Genghis Khan's popularity, he suddenly stopped making games and went to study at the Beijing Film Academy... He had gone off to play with movies!

Watching Chen Guiliang walk away, Shang Jin thought to himself: How did he know I was unhappy at Sohu?

(End of Chapter)
